runs.text: nunciar o Bonzo dez vezes eſte nome em-

lines.note: Nunciar completes Pro-nunciar from f295. The Bonzo pronounces the name ten times while teaching the invocation; em- begins the next divided word. The visible ſ/t ligature is represented with long ſ.

runs.text: ſinando o a inuocar aos que ſe fazem Iǒdoxùs

lines.note: Continues the pronunciation instruction, with fazem and the embedded Iǒdoxùs. Enlarged inspection confirms the first-o caron and the grave over u; the entire Portuguese row is italic.

runs.text: ou querem receber alguã maneira de benção.

lines.note: The continuation concerns receiving a kind of blessing. Enlargement resolves one definite nasal mark over the a of alguã; the faint spot above u is not treated as a second tilde. This chosen reading is recorded as a nonblocking caveat.
After &c., juunen wo vquru begins the reciprocal action: receiving the ten invocations. Reſponderẽ starts the explanation of the response.

runs.text: eſtes Iǒdoxùs ao Bonzo dez vezes inuocando

lines.note: The Iǒdoxùs respond to the Bonzo by invoking the name ten times. Both first-o caron and u grave are visible independently of the occurrence above; no internal roman/italic split is warranted. The visible ſ/t ligature is represented with long ſ.

runs.text: Amida aßi como o Bonzo lhes enſina.

lines.note: Amida completes the invoked name, repeated as the Bonzo teaches. Amida and Bonzo occur within the Portuguese explanation and are eligible for whole-word typeface review.
Junget is an intercalary month, vruzzuqi. The Portuguese begins an explanation of an added lunar month; the final checked t is preserved.

runs.text: crecenta de mais cada tres annos.

lines.note: The compiler describes an extra month added every three years. This is the dictionary’s historical calendrical explanation, not a modern exact rule supplied by the reviewer.
Jungi and jungina mean conforming to right principle, guini xitagǒ. The initial is capital I rather than OCR long ſ, and cõ-forme crosses the physical break.

runs.text: forme à rezão, ou couſa recta, & juſta.

lines.note: Completes conforme and explains conformity to reason, rectitude and justice. The printed rezão is retained rather than modernized. The visible ſ/t ligature is represented with long ſ.
Iunguiacu contrasts the right side with the reverse, then just with unjust. The italic Iuſto has capital I and a long-ſ/t ligature, not a modernized J.

runs.text: injuſto. ¶ Item, No Ximo ẽ todo caſo.

lines.note: Completes injuſto and adds the regional Ximo usage, “in any case.” The tilde belongs to ẽ, and the paragraph sign begins the added sense on this same row.
A short cross-reference from Iunguina to Iungui; both Japanese forms remain roman, with only Vide italic.
Suguni yuqu explains going straight along a road. The final direi- is visibly broken onto the following row, not part of the Japanese synonym.
Completes direito and starts the celestial-motion example Tenno junguiǒ guiacuguiǒni-; both long-vowel marks and the terminal hyphen are retained.

runs.text: Em quanto o ceo ſe mouer des

lines.note: Itarumade continues the example. The Portuguese begins “while heaven moves”; its final des is printed without a hyphen before the next row’s do.

runs.text: do oriente pera opoente, & de hum polo pera

lines.note: Continues the motion from east to west and from one pole toward the other; pera and the tight opoente are retained rather than modernized.
Completes the celestial-motion gloss, then repeats Iunguiǒ for the figurative sense of walking in virtue. The paragraph sign is internal, not a new physical row.
Completes the figurative gloss with pello caminho da virtude; the entire continuation is italic and indented.
The scan reads Iǔni fitoye, not Fini: a long-u mark and the following ni are visible. The gloss introduces the twelve-layer garment worn by court women.
Completes the clothing gloss with the women who serve the Dairi. Dairi is embedded in the Portuguese explanation; molheres and ſeruem are historical spellings.
Iunji gives the verb forms uru, ita and the sense of admission to a rank. Xuc- begins the Japanese religious-rank example across the line break.
Qeno completes Xucqeno; curaini junjeraruru is followed by the italic translation “to be admitted.” The hanging indentation belongs to the preceding entry.
Completes admission to religious dignity and introduces Ta coreni as another example. The paragraph sign does not start a separate physical row.

runs.text: As de mais couſasſão como eſtas.

lines.note: The example ends junzu, with u rather than the draft’s a. Its gloss says the other things are like these; the close setting of couſasſão is retained. The visible ſ/t ligature is represented with long ſ.

runs.text: S. ¶ Item, Correr o ſangue liuremente

lines.note: S. precedes a paragraph sign and an additional sense, blood flowing freely. The entire row is an italic continuation, not another headword.
Completes the blood-flow sense and gives Chiga jũzuru: the small horizontal nasal mark over u is visible. The example is roman after italic Vt.
Iǔniji, Iǔnijichu and Iǔnitoqi all show a caron over their first u. The gloss starts the explanation of twelve day-and-night time divisions.

runs.text: horas do dia, & da noite: cada hũa hora tem

lines.note: The italic continuation says each of those hours contains two hours. The tildes of hũa and the colon after noite remain as printed.
Completes duas and explains that Iǔniji means a natural day. The word aßi is wholly italic; Iǔniji is wholly roman, not split across typefaces.
Completes natural and specifies 24. horas. The number’s following point is retained, with no modern revision of the historical explanation.

runs.text: Dentro de 24. horas. i, de dia,

lines.note: Iǔnijichǔ is glossed as within twenty-four hours, by day and night. The apparent b in the draft’s boras is the italic h of horas.
Completes the day-and-night expression; an entirely italic continuation with its final point.
The initial is I, giving Iǔnino tebaco, not Aǔnino. The Portuguese introduces a woman’s box or small case and divides molheres at the row end.

runs.text: res que tem doze bocetas dentro, ſeis a hũa

lines.note: Completes molheres and states that the case contains twelve smaller boxes, six on one side. Both sixes are distributed over this and the next row.
Completes the arrangement: six on the other side. This is an italic continuation, not a separate definition.

runs.text: Doze veas que ha nos pès, & nas

lines.note: Iǔniqei is defined here as twelve veins in the feet and hands. Preserve the historical medical gloss rather than silently substituting modern terminology.

runs.text: mãos de que falão os medicos. Vt,

lines.note: Completes the reference to physicians and starts the example Iǔniqei, with the comma still at the right edge.
The continuation reads jǔgoracu, without the draft’s extra i, then Vide Iugoracu. The unmarked u in that cross-reference is retained independently of the marked example.
Iunjucu is followed by i, Vagǒ ſuru and a gloss of uniting in friendship. The initial I and the comma after i are visible; the explanation continues below.
Completes Iunjucu with agreement in the same opinion. Restored the continuation indentation visible in the scan.
The headword is Iǔnixǒ, without the draft’s extra i. The gloss explicitly prints 12. Familias after “twelve tribes”; the numeral is not ra or a typeface change.

runs.text: ura que não ha propriamente em Iapão, mas

lines.note: Continues the gloss’s observation that this word is not properly established in Japan. Restored the hanging indent; Iapão is italic with the rest of the explanation.

runs.text: vſa ſe nos liuros da Igreja.

lines.note: Completes the observation with use in Church books. The historical separation vſa ſe is retained and the continuation indent restored.
Iunni introduces the adverb “in order” or “orderly.” It starts at the entry margin, unlike its three following continuation rows.
Adds “rectly” and starts Sacazzuqiuo junni ma-, the example of circulating a sake cup. Restored the indent and retained the visible hyphen.

runs.text: Correr com o Sacazzuqui à roda hum

lines.note: Uaſu completes the verb. The gloss reads Correr com o Sacazzuqui à roda hum: the double r and small spaces are visible; Sacazzuqui occurs within the Portuguese sentence.
The final row reads por hum, not Ior hum. It completes the one-by-one circulation of the cup and sits above the bottom rule with the continuation indent.

A new, unindented entry prints Iǔno without a mark on its final o, although Touono nô and the right-end example Iǔnô have circumflexes. Preserve that anomaly; the supplied NINJAL index independently flags this headword as a misprint. The missing Vt, Iǔnô is restored from the scan.
The example continues xichigueino taxxita fito, including the e of guei (“arts”), then i, and the italic translation. The draft’s guci is a misreading of guei.
Completes conſumado em todas as artes, the accomplished-person gloss. The whole row is italic and indented.

runs.text: O correr cõ o Sacazzuqui por ordẽ por

lines.note: Iunpai is a fresh headword, so its false indent is removed. The Portuguese describes passing the Sacazzuqui in order; the latter is embedded in the italic explanation.
Continues the cup-passing definition with Sazzuqiuo junpaini ſuru. Preserve Sazzuqiuo as actually printed rather than expanding it from the preceding Sacazzuqui.

runs.text: Vento proſpero, ou a popa. Vt,

lines.note: The new headword is Iunpǔ, favorable wind. The example begins Iũ at the extreme right, with a nasal tilde; it remains wholly roman and has no added hyphen.
The split example continues pǔni fouo fiqu, l, caquru, with a caron on u. The italic gloss begins “set sail”; the alternative marker is a lower-case l.
Completes the gloss with a wind astern; the historical unaccented a popa is retained.
Iunquai begins at the headword margin, not at a hanging indent. Iunno quai is a separate synonym and the gloss divides muitos after mui-.

runs.text: tos de diuerſo grao, & dignidade correndo to

lines.note: Continues the invitation of people of differing rank and dignity. The final to is the first part of todos, but no terminal hyphen is visible or supplied.

runs.text: dos pouco a pouco por ſua ordẽ, & por ſua vez.

lines.note: Completes todos and says the invitations proceed little by little in order and in turn. The rightmost full stop is visible and restored.
Iunquan, Xitagai meguru, is glossed Rodear. The damaged narrow i after X is consistent with the full word; no letter or extra word is added.
Tenno junquan is translated as the revolution of the heavens. The transition from roman example to italic explanation occurs after the point.

runs.text: ¶ Item, O correr o ſangue liuremente pellas

lines.note: A paragraph sign adds the circulation of blood as another sense. Retain pellas independently of the earlier pollas on this page.
Completes the blood-circulation gloss with the veins of the body. The row is a short italic continuation.
Iunrei, Meguri vogamu, is glossed as pilgrim or romeiro; the latter is physically split after ro-.
Completes romeiro and adds Iunrei ſuru, “make a pilgrimage.” The final Vt, introduces the next row’s citation example.
Dǒtǒno junrei xite is followed by the roman citation label Feiq. and italic Lib. 4. The last character is the numeral 4, not the draft’s q.

runs.text: Andando em romaria vendo as Teras, ou ermi-

lines.note: The citation gloss describes visiting Teras or hermitages. Teras is embedded in Portuguese; the line ends with the printed ermi- division.

runs.text: das, & torres altas, onde eſtão Fotoques.

lines.note: Completes ermidas, then mentions high towers containing Fotoques. Fotoques is an embedded Japanese plural in the italic explanation.

runs.text: O correr do ſangue liuremente pelas

lines.note: Iunriǔ is the free flow of blood. The draft’s liuremenie is corrected to liuremente by the visible t; the historical statement is retained as a lexical gloss.
The continuation reads veas. Palaura de medicos, not meduos; the separate i and c strokes are legible.
Iunro, with alternative jundǒ, means a straight road. The paragraph sign introduces a metaphorical sense continued below.

runs.text: per met. Caminho recto, ou caminho da vir-

lines.note: The italic per met. labels the figurative sense, a straight path or the way of virtue; vir- remains at the physical line end.
Completes virtude and gives Iunrona fito with its translation as an upright man. The trailing comma connects to the next row.
Completes the upright-person gloss with “and just.” The printed short continuation is preserved, not absorbed into the preceding row. The visible ſ/t ligature is represented with long ſ.
Iuntacu is a short independent headword defined as abundance; the new entry’s margin position is preserved.
Iuntacuna is the adjectival form. The paragraph example divides Yorozzu after Yoroz-, with the second z on the next row.
Completes Yorozzu juntacuna and translates it as having everything in abundance. The nasal mark lies over u in abũdancia.

Iuntacuni. Adu. occupies the left of this physical row; the displaced italic ( materiaes. is at the far right above the Iuntan yen entry. Both are retained on this row using named far-right segments. The intervening draft row was an OCR duplicate/garble, not another printed line.

Iuntan yen is a compound medicine made of many materials. Its final word materiaes. is physically displaced above-right and retained on c2-l030, not duplicated here. Preserve the visible Iuntan even though the supplied lexical index reports an intended Iuntai.
The initial is I, giving Iunvocu, followed by Vruuô iye. The gloss defines a rich and prosperous house; the circumflex over ô remains as printed.
Iunxi and its adjectival alternative junxina describe something upright and orderly. The lower-case l is the alternative marker, not an extra headword letter.
The paragraph example Iunxina fito is translated as an upright, orderly man. Keep the row indented under Iunxi, even though it starts with a paragraph sign.
Iunxocu begins with fresh color or freshness, then Tomaſe introduces an extended sense that continues over two rows.

runs.text: por graça, ou beneficio, que vem do ceo, ou

lines.note: Continues the extended sense as grace or benefit coming from heaven. The following ou connects to the high-ranking person on the next row.
Completes the source of a benefit as some high-ranking person, followed by S. The nasal mark is over u in dalgũa; the historical peßoa spelling is retained.
Iunyen, Xitagǒ yen, begins an explanation in terms of connection or combination. Liãça is the printed contracted form, not silently expanded to a modern equivalent.

runs.text: de que hum he leuado. ¶ Item, Obras q̃

lines.note: Completes the connection by which someone is led, then adds Obras q̃. The mark after Item is a comma, and the abbreviation carries its tilde over q.

runs.text: deſi direitamente são boas, & bem ordenadas.

lines.note: Completes the second sense with works that are good in themselves and well ordered. The scan visibly indents the row, so the provisional flush-left setting is corrected.
This headword reads Iuqiô, with circumflex rather than caron, as does Qiôni iru. The gloss concerns pleasure or delight in something, not the following homographic doctrine entry.
Completes the pleasure gloss and starts Iuqiôno amarini aſobi. The circumflex and the restored continuation indent are both visible.
Tauamururu completes the Japanese example; the italic gloss concerns recreation and diversion while feeling excessive delight. The printed eſtã- division remains at the right edge.
Completes the recreation gloss with excess of delight and pleasure. Restored the hanging indent and retained the entirely italic row.
A separate Iuqiô entry, again with circumflex, gives Iuxano voxiye and introduces moral doctrine. The final q̃ belongs to the italic Portuguese explanation.
Completes the doctrine entry with certain philosophers of China. Restored the visible continuation indent and retained the capital Philoſophos.
The initial is I, giving Iuracu, Miyacoye iru, “enter the Miyaco.” Miyaco is also embedded in the italic Portuguese gloss; the entry ends before the catchword.
